name: Technical Brutalist
when: Developer tools, infra, portfolios that want to signal raw competence over polish.
anti: Do not soften with big shadows or rounded blobs — that breaks the concept.

name: Refined Dark (House Default)
when: Default when the brief wants premium/advanced/standout SaaS or product UI.
anti: No loud flat accent fills, no bouncy motion — restraint is the identity.

name: Editorial
when: Blogs, long-form, brand and agency sites where type and reading are the product.
anti: Avoid dashboard density; let it breathe.

name: Minimal Modern
when: Marketing/SaaS that wants clean, trustworthy, current — the safe-but-good default light theme.
anti: Heavy borders and drop-shadows make it feel like a form, not a product.

name: Glass / Depth
when: AI, futuristic, or premium product surfaces that benefit from translucency and depth.
anti: Overdone blur kills contrast/legibility — keep text on solid enough backing.

name: Bento Grid
when: Feature overviews, dashboards, product landing sections showing many capabilities at once.
signatures: modular boxed cells of varied size
anti: Equal-weight cells with no focal point read as a spreadsheet.

name: Warm Organic
when: Wellness, hospitality, food, boutique commerce — human and inviting.
anti: Cold grays or sharp brutalist edges fight the warmth.

name: Cinematic Bold
when: Entertainment, media, launch/campaign sites where mood and impact win.
anti: Do not bury the message under effects — impact needs a clear focal claim.
